subject: Error when manually creating IOU and BM objects

messages.author: e520c41c6310fbe3
messages.subject: Error when manually creating IOU and BM objects
parts:
I have been following Appendix S3 in Calabrese et al. (2016) to creat and plot variograms from IOU and BM objects (tau velocity taken from variogram.fit), but I get the following error(s):
> vg <- variogram(F61.1997, fast=FALSE)

> variogram.fit(vg)
> iou <- ctmm(tau=c(Inf, 3.5))
> bm <- ctmm(tau=Inf)
> summary(iou)
Error in summary.ctmm.single(object, level = level, level.UD = level.UD,  : 
  trying to get slot "par" from an object of a basic class ("NULL") with no slots

> plot(vg, CTMM=iou, col.CTMM = "#1b9e77")
Error in unit.ctmm(CTMM[[i]], length = sqrt(SVF.scale), time = lag.scale) : 
  trying to get slot "par" from an object of a basic class ("numeric") with no slots

However, the models do seem to be present, as evidenced by:
> IOU_F61.1997 <- ctmm.fit(F61.1997, iou)
> summary(IOU_F61.1997)
$CI
                       low           ML         high
tau velocity (seconds)   0 3.375706e-04     3.255743
speed (kilometers/day)   0 4.090274e+02 40169.375327

I have tried specifying the tau(velocity) units with %#%, but got the same error. It seems like I'm missing something simple. Any suggestions?
Thanks,
Roy

messages.author: 40fd627580dd34f5
messages.subject: Re: Error when manually creating IOU and BM objects
parts:
Hi Roy,

ctmm() creates a prototype/guess of the model, which is not necessarily complete. In this case, iou and bm aren't specified enough for summary() or plot.variogram() to work. You can run them through ctmm.guess() and ctmm.fit() with the data to flesh out the remaining parameters, like you did with IOU_F61.1997. plot.variogram() should work with CTMM=IOU_F61.1997.

Here summary() and plot.variogram() are both failing because they are looking for diffusion rate information, which was never specified (sigma in variogram.fit).

Best,
Chris

messages.author: 40fd627580dd34f5
messages.subject: Re: Error when manually creating IOU and BM objects
parts:
Hi Roy,

My suspicion is that you can't compare them because the IOU likelihood contains dependence on a prior (which we derive from the limit of a large OUF model)... and that prior is probably doing something beyond standard likelihood analysis.

However, you could look at the sampling distribution of tau_velocity, which when zero makes IOU become BM.

Best,
Chris
